title: Controllability
equipment: Two equal gravity-drained tanks and one upstream pump
physicalPurpose: Observe direct and propagated influence of the same bounded upstream pump.
principalTechnique: Controllability matrix and bounded physical pulse experiments
objective: Distinguish local transient controllability from holding arbitrary unequal steady levels.

simplifications: Equal fixed cross sections and discharge coefficients; free upstream discharge without downstream backpressure.
Physical levels use coupled RK4 gravity balances; the ST predictor is a separate local one-second Euler approximation.

baseline.limitation: Local transient controllability does not establish arbitrary unequal steady-state levels.

change.decision: Compare opposite bounded pulse responses while preserving the same equilibrium and physical model.

disturbances: Separate fresh h1=h2=.25 m cases use +.001 and −.001 m3/s pump deviations for20s, then restore .010m3/s for100s.

abortPredicates: Level outside .05–.45 m, requested flow outside0–.020 m3/s, invalid data or a non-one-second clock interval.
safety.restorationMode: Normal completion restores .010 m3/s; early abort commands zero and requires simulator stop/reset.
simulationOnlyRestrictions: The result is simulation evidence for this lesson model.

video.viewerOutcome: Distinguish local transient controllability from holding arbitrary unequal steady levels.

learning.context: The two state equations preserve upstream and downstream water storage.
learning.reason: One pump acts directly upstream; its effect reaches downstream later.
theory: B=[2,0] and AB=[−.08,.08] span two local transient directions. Equal steady levels remain required by the downstream balance.
learning.workedPrediction: The determinant2*.08−0*(−.08)=.16 is nonzero; the input can influence both local transient state directions.
practicalPreparation: Reset both physical levels to .25m and pump flow to .010m3/s.
learning.change: Use Control Studio to display B, AB and rank, then compare opposite physical pump pulses.
learning.comparison: After a full reset, apply−.001m3/s for20s.
learning.validation: Inspect bounded same-sign direct/upstream and delayed/downstream deviations; do not infer arbitrary steady targets.
learning.explanation: Controllability concerns independent transient directions under the local model, with physical constraints considered separately.
learning.transfer: Observability asks whether downstream measurement history distinguishes both states.
